title: What Is Salary Sacrifice Australia? Hourly to Annual Pay Guide
description: Learn what is salary sacrifice Australia and how it affects your hourly to annual conversion. Includes tax, super, minimum wage, and award rates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is calculated as hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice affect my superannuation?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice reduces your pre-tax salary, which may lower the ordinary earnings base on which the 12% super guarantee is calculated. However, you can also sacrifice into super to boost your retirement savings. The Australian Taxation Office sets limits on concessional contributions. Our calculator does not include salary sacrifice; it assumes no sacrifice and estimates super at 12% of ordinary earnings up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries or occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Most employees are covered by an award. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2%. Our estimate uses these rates with the full tax-free threshold and the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare. It does not include HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives the formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, at the [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. Your fortnightly pay would be roughly $26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.44 before tax and super.

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, most employees are covered by an award – a legal minimum for their industry or role. Award rates are often higher than the national minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award.

If you are a casual worker, you should never type a rate that already includes casual loading into the timesheet. Instead, enter your base hourly rate and check the box to add 25% casual loading. The calculator will apply it correctly.

## Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an employee earning the National Minimum Wage, the employer would contribute an additional $6,269.45 per year (12% of $52,245.44) into your super fund.

Now, you might be wondering: **what is salary sacrifice australia**? Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. This reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering the tax you pay. However, it can also reduce the ordinary earnings base for your super guarantee, unless the sacrifice is made directly into super. The Australian Taxation Office regulates salary sacrifice and sets caps on concessional contributions.

Our calculator does not include salary sacrifice. It assumes your full hourly rate is ordinary earnings. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Our estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or any salary packaging.

For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,245.44), the tax would be approximately:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on next $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on remaining $7,245.44 ($45,001 to $52,245.44) = $2,173.63
- Total tax = $6,193.63
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,044.91
- Total tax and Medicare = $7,238.54
- Take-home pay ≈ $45,006.90 per year, or about $865.52 per week.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Knowing your fortnightly pay can help with budgeting. Multiply your weekly gross by 2. For the National Minimum Wage: $1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight before tax. After tax and Medicare, the fortnightly take-home would be roughly $1,731.03.

## Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/) on our home page lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, tick the box to add 25% casual loading. The calculator will show your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, super, and take-home pay. Remember, super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings and is not deducted from your pay.

For more detailed comparisons, see our [reference tables](/data) and guides on [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion). The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That is an average across all industries, not a median for any specific job.

## Important Disclaimer

This guide provides estimates only. Your actual pay, tax, and super depend on your specific circumstances, including your award, hours, and any salary sacrifice arrangements. Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for pay rates and the Australian Taxation Office for tax obligations.
